narr: In a moisture rich environment, with above normal PWATs and high mixing ratios, slow-moving thunderstorms in the the morning of the 10th produced very heavy rainfall, with rain rates upwards of 2 to 2.5 inches per hour, leading to localized flash flooding in parts of Maricopa and Pinal counties. Impacts included flowing washes and even a flooded exit ramp in Chandler.
ev: Loop 202 westbound exit ramp to Gilbert Road in Chandler was closed due to flooding. Nearby Chandler Airport measured 2.68 inches of rain from approximately 0700MST to 0900MST with 2.13 inches falling in 1 hour. The exit ramp did not re-open until around 1100MST. No injuries or damages were reported.

A streamflow gage on Vekol Wash at Ralston Road experienced a 2 foot rise in roughly 25 to 30 minutes, from 0.15 feet at 1154MST to 2.14 feet at 1220MST. A webcam from the gage showed Ralston Road was impassable to traffic. The flood waters originated several miles upstream from thunderstorms just south of Interstate-8 (I-8) near the Pinal and Maricopa county border. A streamflow gage on Vekol wash near I-8 also registered a 2 foot rise in roughly 1 hour, from 4.95 feet (base value) at 0720MST to 6.94 feet (crest) at 0816MST. Radar estimated rainfall in the area of Vekol wash and I-8 was around 1 inch. Flood waters took roughly 4 hours to travel from I-8 to Ralston Road. Although not reported, Val Vista Road, Peters and Nall Road, and Farrell Road may have also experienced impacts. No damages or injuries were reported.
